topic: Wide and narrow scope negation with degree adjuncts
claim: After setting aside metalinguistic negation, the text says “In what follows we ignore cases of this kind and consider below only narrow scope ordinary negation.”
evidence_summary: The cases discussed next all have the adjunct inside the scope of the negative; the first is [22] (p. 724), labelled “[adjunct in scope of negation]”. Page 724 uses the term for the opposite configuration: “Nevertheless, narrow scope negation is not entirely excluded”, with [24] labelled “[negation in scope of adjunct]”. Ch. 9 p. 793 fixes the convention: “in [23ii] the negative has narrow scope relative to the adjunct, whereas in [23iii] it has wide scope”, and [23iii] is labelled “[negative has scope over adjunct]”.
finding: The text means wide scope negation: the discussion that follows concerns negation with scope over the adjunct, which p. 724 and Ch. 9 call wide scope. Reading the phrase as ordinary negation in which the adjunct has narrow scope doesn’t work, since p. 724 uses the same collocation for the opposite reading.
proposed_wording: consider below only wide scope ordinary negation
inference: Does the discussion that follows concern narrow scope negation?

evidence.passage: §11, p. 725. “consider below only narrow scope ordinary negation”
evidence.establishes: The term names the opposite of the configuration discussed.
